s1-hidden-stor.base: STOR must behave as specified when driven through its entry point STOR_AppMain with software bus messages, using only the names, structures, message IDs, function codes and event IDs in the specification.

cases.S1 Startup and housekeeping: at startup STOR must register events and the StorageTable (400 bytes) with a validation function, subscribe to its command, SEND_HK and WAKEUP message IDs, every used table entry and the global STOR_XFER_SEG_MID and STOR_XFER_ACK_MID, create both roots one directory level at a time, emit event 1, and answer SEND_HK with the 72-byte STOR_HkTlm_Payload_t including the idle transfer fields
cases.S1 Heartbeat: STOR must send one SFI_HeartbeatCmd_t on SFI_HEARTBEAT_MID on every 1 Hz WAKEUP, with AppName STOR and Sequence 1 for the first heartbeat and one more for each next one
cases.S1 Startup error events: initialization and pipe failures must be reported with events 7 (pipe), 8 (table registration), 9 (table load), 11 (subscription) and 12 (directory creation)
cases.S1 Table validation: the table validation function must reject empty or unterminated roots, zero quotas, MaxPacketFileBytes below 1024 or above TelemetryQuotaBytes, a threshold outside 1..100, a used entry with Priority or Decimation 0 and duplicate used MsgIds (event 10), and accept the boundary values
cases.S1 Decimation and statistics: an entry stores a packet (command or telemetry) only when (Received - 1) % Decimation is 0, counting the rest as Decimated; SEND_STATS reports Received, Stored, Decimated, Dropped, Priority and Decimation per entry; SET_DECIMATION and SET_PRIORITY take effect at run time with event 16
cases.S1 Packet files and roll-over: packet files are named tlm_<MMMM>_<NNNNNNNN>.bin under TelemetryRoot, start with a CFE_FS_Header_t of sub type 0x5354 and description "STOR packet file", hold the packets exactly as received, roll over before a packet would exceed MaxPacketFileBytes (exactly filling it is allowed), and CLOSE_FILES closes them with event 27
cases.S1 Startup scan and sequence: at startup STOR deletes every *.part file of the file area, initializes TelemetryBytesUsed from the existing .bin and .arc packet files and FileBytesUsed and FileCount from the regular files, and continues each MID's packet file sequence from the highest existing sequence (archived files included) plus one
cases.S1 Purge order: when TelemetryBytesUsed exceeds the threshold, closed packet files are deleted one at a time, lowest priority first and lowest sequence first, never an open file, with FilesPurged and PurgeCycles counted
cases.S1 Purge of archived files: archived (.arc) packet files are purged before any .bin file, each group by lowest current priority (0 for a MID no longer in the table) and lowest sequence, and they count in TelemetryBytesUsed
cases.S1 Purge after priority change: run-time SET_PRIORITY and SET_PURGE_THRESHOLD change which files are purged first
cases.S1 Telemetry quota drops: a packet that would take TelemetryBytesUsed over TelemetryQuotaBytes is dropped (Dropped, PacketsDropped) with event 13 once per entry until it stores again, and SET_PURGE_THRESHOLD frees space
cases.S1 Parameter commands: SET_PRIORITY, SET_DECIMATION (value 0 or unknown MsgId) and SET_PURGE_THRESHOLD (outside 1..100) are rejected with event 17 and a command error; valid values are accepted with event 16
cases.S1 Command errors: an invalid function code gives event 2, a wrong command length event 6, an unknown message ID event 5, each counted as a command error
cases.S1 Command counters: every accepted command (including SEND_STATS, LIST_DIR, LIST_ALL, CLOSE_FILES and the file commands) increments CommandCounter, and every rejected one increments CommandErrorCounter and nothing else
cases.S1 Reset counters: RESET_COUNTERS zeroes the command, packet, purge and file-add counters and all per-entry counters without touching byte accounting, FileCount, open files or run-time parameters
cases.S1 File add and delete: ADD_FILE copies the source into the file area creating directories (event 22) and rejects an existing destination (20), an unreadable source (19) and a quota overrun (21, FileAddsRejected, no partial file); DELETE_FILE removes a regular file (24) and reports a missing file or directory (23)
cases.S1 Path rejection: file area paths containing .. or starting with / are rejected with event 18 for ADD_FILE, DELETE_FILE and LIST_DIR without changing anything
cases.S1 Listing packets: LIST_DIR and LIST_ALL send STOR_ListTlm_t packets of at most four entries with TotalEntries, PacketIndex and EntriesInPacket, directories as name/ with size 0, LIST_ALL depth-first with relative paths, an empty listing as one packet, and event 25 for a missing directory
cases.S1 Table update: after a table update STOR subscribes to new entries, unsubscribes from removed ones, keeps its transfer subscriptions, and resets the run-time priority, decimation and threshold to the table values
cases.S1 Idle close: on WAKEUP a packet file not written for 10 seconds or more is closed, and not earlier
cases.S1 File write failures: a packet file that cannot be created or written is reported with event 15 and STOR keeps running

s2-hidden-stor-transfer.base: STOR transfers must behave as specified when STOR is driven through its entry point STOR_AppMain with software bus messages, using only the names, structures, message IDs, function codes, enumerations and event IDs in the specification.

cases.S2 Transfer command rejections: TRANSFER is rejected with STOR_XFER_ERR_EID and a command error, starting nothing, when a transfer is active, Area or SuccessAction is out of range, Destination is the own node ID, Path breaks the path rules or (telemetry area) is not exactly a packet file name, the source is missing, a directory or an open packet file, or a peer DestPath is empty, unterminated or breaks the path rules; wrongly sized TRANSFER and ABORT_TRANSFER commands give event 6
cases.S2 Ground transfer of a stored file: an accepted ground TRANSFER sets XferState SENDING and XferActiveId (1 for the first TRANSFER, +1 per TRANSFER) with event 29, sends nothing before the next WAKEUP, then sends full-size STOR_XferTlm_t segments on STOR_XFER_TLM_MID with TransferId, SrcNode, DstNode 0, Area, SegmentIndex, SegmentCount, FileSize, the CRC-32/ISO-HDLC FileCrc, Offset, DataLength, DestPath (the source Path) and zero-filled unused Data, and completes after the last segment (XfersCompleted, XferLastStatus OK, XferState IDLE, event 31, XferSegmentsSent)
cases.S2 Segmentation pacing and empty files: at most STOR_XFER_SEGS_PER_WAKEUP (8) segments are sent per WAKEUP, in index order, and a zero-length file is one segment with DataLength 0
cases.S2 Peer transfer and acknowledgement: a peer transfer sends full-size STOR_XferSegCmd_t commands (function code 0) on STOR_XFER_SEG_MID with DstNode the destination, then waits in AWAITING_ACK; STOR ignores its own segments on its local bus without counting them, ignores acknowledgements whose TransferId, SrcNode or DstNode do not match, and completes on a matching OK acknowledgement
cases.S2 Acknowledgement failure and timeout: a matching acknowledgement with another status fails the transfer with that status (XfersFailed, XferLastStatus, STOR_XFER_FAIL_ERR_EID, no success action), and with no acknowledgement within STOR_XFER_ACK_TIMEOUT wakeups after the last segment the transfer fails with TIMEOUT, without resending
cases.S2 Abort transfer: ABORT_TRANSFER with a transfer active (sending or awaiting the acknowledgement) fails it with ABORTED and STOR_XFER_ABORT_INF_EID instead of STOR_XFER_FAIL_ERR_EID and stops its segments; with none active it is rejected with STOR_XFER_ERR_EID
cases.S2 Success actions in the file area: DELETE removes the source with DELETE_FILE accounting, MARK_ARCHIVED renames <Path> to <Path>.arc without changing FileBytesUsed or FileCount, and a MARK_ARCHIVED that fails because <Path>.arc exists still completes the transfer with XferLastStatus ACTION_FAILED and STOR_XFER_ACTION_ERR_EID
cases.S2 Success actions for packet files: a packet file transfer sends the file's bytes with Area TLM; MARK_ARCHIVED renames tlm_MMMM_NNNNNNNN.bin to .arc keeping TelemetryBytesUsed and leaves a .arc name unchanged; DELETE removes the packet file with its bytes subtracted but without the purge counters
cases.S2 Source read error: a source read error during sending fails the transfer with IO and STOR_XFER_FAIL_ERR_EID, without the success action
cases.S2 Receiving a file: a segment with index 0 addressed to this node starts an inbound transfer writing <FileRoot>/<DestPath>.part (directories created, RxState RECEIVING, .part bytes not counted); after the last segment with a matching CRC the file is renamed to DestPath, FileCount, FileBytesUsed, FilesReceived and XferSegmentsReceived are updated, STOR_XFER_RX_INF_EID is sent and an acknowledgement OK with BytesReceived goes out on STOR_XFER_ACK_MID with SrcNode this node and DstNode the sender
cases.S2 Receiver rejections: the receiver NAKs PATH (bad DestPath or a final component plus .part over 31 characters), EXISTS, QUOTA, SEQUENCE (not the next index), CRC (after the last segment) and IO (write or rename failure); every NAK deletes the partial file, increments RxErrors, sends STOR_XFER_RX_ERR_EID and an acknowledgement with that status
cases.S2 Receiver timeout and restart: no segment for STOR_XFER_RX_TIMEOUT wakeups aborts an inbound transfer without acknowledgement (partial file deleted, RxErrors, STOR_XFER_RX_ERR_EID); a new index 0 discards an incomplete inbound transfer without acknowledging it, and segments of another (SrcNode, TransferId) with a nonzero index are ignored without counting
cases.S2 Segments addressed elsewhere: segments and acknowledgements whose DstNode is not this node are ignored, without counting, acknowledging or a command error
cases.S2 Transfer counters and reset: RESET_COUNTERS zeroes XfersCompleted, XfersFailed, XferSegmentsSent, XferSegmentsReceived, FilesReceived and RxErrors but not XferActiveId, XferLastStatus, the transfer state or the file accounting
